name: Vectors / relationship diagram
oneLine: The arrows drawn between two people's PAC diagrams showing which ego state sent a message and which one it was aimed at.
whatYouDid: You drew the stimulus vector from Priya's Adult to Arjun's Adult, and the response vector back the same way - the parallel arrows were what told you the transaction was complementary, not the words alone.
confusion: The easy mistake isn't a specific wrong answer - it's skipping the diagram altogether and trying to diagnose a transaction from the words alone, when the vectors are what actually settle it.

fromBook.quote: The arrows show the direction of each communication. In formal language, these arrows are known as vectors.

expand.definition: Each ego state (Parent, Adult, Child) on one person's diagram can send to, or be addressed by, any of the three on the other person's diagram - the full relationship diagram is the set of vectors a transaction could travel between two three-circle stacks. There are nine such possible vectors in all.
expand.otherFraming: Whether a transaction is complementary or crossed is read entirely off the vectors - parallel vectors landing on the state that answers mean complementary; vectors that aren't parallel, or that land somewhere else, mean crossed.
expand.tryThisToday: Next time you're diagnosing an exchange, physically sketch the two PAC stacks and draw the arrow before you decide what kind of transaction it is - the shape usually makes the answer obvious.
